methods.label: Direct multiplication

methods.label: Grouping eight boxes at a time
methods.explanation: Group the 16 boxes into two groups of 8 so that each group has a round total: \(125\times8=1000\) bottles. The two groups therefore contain \(1000\times2=2000\) bottles altogether.
methods.levelReason: Grouping factors and calculating these whole-number products are within Grade 4 scope.

review.mathematicalCheck: Method 1 gives the correct product, 2000. Independently, Method 2 partitions all 16 boxes into two groups of eight: each contains 125 × 8 = 1000 bottles, so the total is 1000 × 2 = 2000. Both explanations are sufficient for this calculation.
review.levelCheck: Both methods use Grade 4 multiplication; the alternative's concrete grouping explains the associativity involved.
review.methodDistinctness: Grouping eight boxes to make 1000 supplies a useful calculation idea beyond the retained direct equation and requires no advanced knowledge.
